summary: Batched multi-tool request: partial side effects when retry splits actions across replicas (Go SDK)
description:
Issue summary: Customer sends a single batched request that includes three tool/function calls in sequence (pay-authorize -> record-ledger -> notify). In ~1% of requests during high concurrency the final two actions are executed only partially: pay-authorize succeeds once, record-ledger runs twice or not at all, and notify is missed. Impact: inconsistent financial and notification state for customers, visible as duplicate ledger entries or missed notifications.

Observed behavior: Walkthrough of a failing trace from PayFlux: the Go SDK client constructs a single multipart request with per-action metadata (action nonces and a per-request transaction-id). Under an autoscaling event, the request appears to be split across two serving replicas (replica A returns an ack for action1 and action2, replica B returns for action3) — but due to nonce rotation on client retry and KV cache warmup on the runtime, a second execution of action2 is observed downstream (duplicate ledger row) while action3's webhook did not fire. Expected behavior: either transactional ordering with single execution per action (at-most-once) or clear guidance that batched multi-tool sequences are not atomic and require customer-side dedup/compensation.

Environment details: Go SDK v0.9.3 (enterprise fork), network: TLS via customer-managed VPC peer, Redwood serving-runtime v2.6.1, autoscaling policy with burst pools enabled in us-east-1.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends a single API call using Go SDK BatchFuncCall that contains three tool invocations in sequence with per-action nonces and transaction-id header.
2) Load generator sends 2000 concurrent batched requests to the same route with short inter-arrival times to trigger autoscaling/burst routing.
3) Artificially inject a transient 500ms delay on replica A's response path (to simulate GC/warmup) using test harness.
4) Observe downstream systems (ledger DB and notification webhook) for duplicates/missing events and collect request/response traces.
5) Compare SDK client-side retry logs and server-side request routing traces for matching transaction-id and action nonces.
logs: CLIENT: [2026-03-10T16:12:43Z] tx-id=tx-89c3 action=pay-authorize nonce=na-17 attempt=1 -> 200 OK
CLIENT: [2026-03-10T16:12:43Z] tx-id=tx-89c3 action=record-ledger nonce=na-18 attempt=1 -> 202 Accepted

comments: 2026-03-10 18:05 UTC - Aisha Patel (Support): Opened with customer's raw traces and downstream evidence. Assigned to Marco for triage.

2026-03-11 09:42 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Reproduced locally with load harness. Observed request split behavior when autoscaler attaches burst replica before KV cache warmup completes. Suspect race between client retry semantics and routing/fallback logic.

2026-03-11 14:10 UTC - PayFlux (Customer): We rely on batched sequences to be effectively ordered for accounting. Duplicate ledger entries cause reconciliation errors. Can you confirm whether batched multi-tool sequences are atomic?

2026-03-12 07:55 UTC - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Short answer: not currently atomic across replicas. The platform aims for at-most-once per action when idempotency metadata is present, but our dedup semantics depend on consistent idempotency key normalization and lifecycle of the idempotency cache across routing fallbacks. We're seeing gaps when retries change per-action nonces or when a request is split mid-flight. Investigation underway to identify deterministic repro and short-term mitigation.
2026-03-13 11:20 UTC - Customer Success (Lina Gomez): Customer seeks recommended mitigation and if immediate config changes are possible (disable burst pool for route, increase sticky routing TTL).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: SDK-side nonce rotation on per-retry path causes idempotency-key mismatch when parts of a batch are retried to different replicas.

Hypothesis 2: Serving runtime can split batches for load reasons; split parts carry the same transaction-id but action-level nonces are expected to be stable; we observed mutation of nonce header on client side during retry callback path.

Logs show replica-A returned accept for first two actions while replica-B later processed the third action; mismatched attempt counters on client show action3 was retried with a different nonce value.
Cache window: idempotency cache TTL is 30s for route; when replica-B was cold the KV cache warmup delayed dedup check long enough for second execution to be accepted (race).
Repro: Deterministic repro achieved in lab by enabling burst pool and injecting 200ms processing jitter; duplicate ledger row & missing webhook reproduced 7/20 runs.
resolution_notes: Workaround provided to customer: 1) Disable burst pool for the impacted route (via Console -> Routing -> RouteSettings -> allow_burst=false) to avoid mid-request split; 2) Set SDK to use stable per-action idempotency keys (client must not rotate action nonces on retry), recommended field: ActionIdempotencyKey derived from transaction-id + action-index.

Short-term platform fix: engineering to add server-side normalization that prefers per-request transaction-id when available and treats missing/rotated action nonces as identical for a short grace window. Patch PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1224 (WIP).

Long-term: design doc proposal to document transactional guarantees for batched multi-action requests; options: explicit 'transactional' mode that pins request to a single replica, or stronger at-most-once semantics via global idempotency index with cross-replica coordination. Draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Batch+Transaction+Spec (in review).

Customer follow-up: CS recommended a reconciliation-safe pattern (idempotency token per high-level transaction + idempotent downstream writes using transaction-id). Customer accepted workaround; will schedule a follow-up after platform patch rollout.
Status: monitoring patch rollout to staging; recommend keeping ticket open until PR merges and customer verifies in staging.
